summary: This file configures PHP CS Fixer, a tool that automatically formats PHP code to follow style standards. It sets up which files to scan (everything except common directories like vendor and node_modules), loads a license header text file, then applies PSR12 coding standards along with a custom license header comment at the top of each PHP file.

explanations.3: PhpCsFixer\Finder::create() starts building an object that will search for PHP files to format.
explanations.4: ->in('.') tells the finder to look in the current directory and everything inside it.
explanations.5: ->exclude() removes certain directories from the search so we don't format third-party code or config files that shouldn't be touched.
explanations.13: file_get_contents() reads the entire license header text file into a string variable so we can add it to the top of PHP files.
explanations.15: new PhpCsFixer\Config() creates a fresh configuration object that we'll customize with our rules.
explanations.17: setRules() tells the fixer what coding style rules to apply when it formats the code.
explanations.19: '@PSR12' => true means use the PSR12 standard, which is an industry-standard set of PHP formatting rules.
explanations.21: rtrim($header, '\r\n') removes trailing line breaks from the license text so it doesn't add extra blank lines.
explanations.27: ->setCacheFile() tells the fixer where to store a cache file so it runs faster on subsequent checks by remembering which files haven't changed.
explanations.28: ->setIndent() configures how many spaces should be used for indentation (four spaces in this case).
explanations.29: ->setLineEnding() ensures all line breaks use Unix-style (\n) instead of Windows (\r\n) or old Mac (\r) style.
explanations.30: ->setFinder() connects the file finder we built earlier so the fixer knows which files to process.
